S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
examples: Makes mistakes in homework or tests by misreading questions or skipping important parts.
Frequently omits details or makes typos in work documents or reports.
Repeats mistakes in calculations or numerical work, such as switching signs or getting digits wrong.
Performs tasks incorrectly by missing important details in instructions.

S002.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
S002.description: Often has difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities.
examples: Focuses at first during class or meetings but soon becomes distracted or spaces out.
Re-reads the same paragraph in a book multiple times but the content does not register.
Loses focus while watching movies or TV and misses the plot.
Unable to maintain attention until the end of a long meeting or lecture, often drifting off or becoming drowsy.

S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
examples: Desk, bag, or room is always messy and remains disorganized.
Unable to prioritize or determine the order of tasks, starting them randomly.
Fails to plan time effectively, frequently missing deadlines or rushing to finish at the last minute.
Feels overwhelmed by how to start multi-step projects and procrastinates.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
examples: Easily distracted and stops working due to small noises or movements nearby.
Cannot concentrate because eyes keep wandering to the scenery outside the window or people passing by.
Starts daydreaming or gets sidetracked by sudden thoughts while working or studying.
Loses focus and listens in when hearing side conversations or TV sounds.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
examples: Forgets appointment times or meeting schedules, arriving late or missing them entirely.
Forgets to reply to received calls or messages for days.
Frequently incurs late fees because of missing deadlines for utility bills or credit card payments.
Forgets to take medication or leaves necessary items at home when going out.

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
examples: Constantly shaking legs or twisting and squirming body while seated.
Spinning a pen or fiddling with nearby objects, unable to keep hands still.
Continually changing posture and feeling uncomfortable while sitting.
Constantly moving, such as tapping the desk with fingers or tapping feet on the floor.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
examples: Feels uncomfortable and restless as if something is squirming inside when sitting still.
Feels internally anxious and stifled in situations requiring prolonged sitting.
A sense of urgency and anxiety that one must keep moving or doing something.
Feels unable to endure staying still and must constantly be doing something.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
examples: Unable to engage in calm activities for long, such as reading quietly or drawing.
Cannot play quietly, often shouting or making loud noises during games or play.
Unable to stay quiet in quiet places like libraries or movie theaters, making noise.
Cannot endure and avoids quiet and calm activities like meditation or yoga.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
examples: Constantly moving and active as if driven by a motor.
Starts another task immediately after finishing one, without resting for a moment.
Unable to stay still even on weekends or days off, constantly doing something.
Appears to others to be always busy and bustling about.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
examples: Cannot wait and cuts in line or gets impatient when standing in a queue.
Rushes or cuts in without waiting for their turn in games or board games.
Keeps checking the time or complaining when waiting for their turn at hospitals or public offices.
Fidgets, complains, or gets annoyed in situations where waiting for a turn is required.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
examples: Butts into conversations of others where they have not been invited.
Joins in on others' work or games without permission or interferes.
Touches or uses other people's belongings or work without permission.
Keeps talking to and disturbing others when they are focusing on work or studying.

info.persona: Josue Rodriguezquiles, a 53‑year‑old IT veteran, marries meticulous troubleshooting with relentless curiosity for vintage radios, while his competitive streak in chess and habit of pulling all‑night Raspberry Pi tinkering sessions reveal a life balanced between disciplined precision and playful improvisation.
info.professional_persona: Josue Rodriguezquiles, a veteran enterprise technical support engineer, leverages over 25 years of Windows and Linux troubleshooting, network configuration, and PowerShell/Bash automation to deliver clear, jargon‑free solutions, while his curiosity‑driven tinkering and pragmatic reliability make him a natural mentor and aspiring senior IT service manager.
info.cultural_background: Born to Mexican immigrant parents, Josue grew up bilingual, speaking Spanish at home and learning English in school. Mexican cultural traditions—including Día de los Muertos, Quinceañeras, and weekend family meals featuring mole, tamales, and fresh tortillas—remain central to his identity. After relocating to Saint Paul, he integrated into the local Hispanic community, volunteering at the Hispanic Cultural Center and participating in cultural festivals that celebrate Mexican heritage. His upbringing instilled a strong work ethic, respect for family, and a commitment to community support, which shape his reliable professional demeanor and his desire to give back through technology education.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Josue enjoys exploring Minnesota's natural trails, especially at Fort Snelling State Park, where he combines hiking with photography to capture seasonal landscapes. He maintains a home workshop for woodworking and vintage radio restoration, satisfying his curiosity about how things work. In the kitchen, he experiments with traditional Mexican dishes—mole, tamales, and ceviche—infusing them with Midwestern ingredients. He is an avid chess player, regularly competing in local club tournaments, and a hobbyist tinkerer with Raspberry Pi projects such as home automation and retro gaming consoles. He also attends jazz and regional Mexican music concerts and spends solitary evenings reading classic science‑fiction novels.
info.sports_persona: Josue Rodriguezquiles enjoys weekend hikes at Fort Snelling State Park for cardio, plays pick‑up basketball at a local community center in the summer, follows the Minnesota Vikings and the Minnesota Timberwolves closely, and is a member of the St. Paul Chess Club, where he often burns off tournament tension with a quick jog around Como Park.
info.arts_persona: Josue Rodriguezquiles blends his love for visual storytelling with a hobbyist eye, snapping sunrise landscapes while listening to Miles Davis and Mariachi Los Camperos, and occasionally attends live performances by the Minnesota Orchestra and local jazz trio The Mint, which fuel his appreciation for improvisation and classic melodies.
info.travel_persona: Josue Rodriguezquiles prefers meticulously planned road trips through the Upper Midwest, such as his recent week‑long excursion to the Boundary Waters Canoe Area, while dreaming of a future cultural immersion tour of Oaxaca and a rugged trek across Patagonia, balancing his love for nature with a modest travel budget and occasional family commitments.
info.culinary_persona: Josue Rodriguezquiles, an avid home chef, mixes traditional mole with locally sourced wild rice, rolls tamales stuffed with Minnesota duck confit, and crafts ceviche using Great Lakes perch, all while experimenting with smoky chipotle and fresh herbs, showcasing his intermediate culinary skill and a penchant for merging regional ingredients with Mexican classics.

info.persona: Tracey Beagles blends her structured budgeting and community‑servant spirit with a love for spontaneous dance, crossword puzzles, and historic travel, navigating senior life with calm resilience and a habit of misplacing knitting needles in the most unlikely places.
info.professional_persona: Tracey Beagles, a retired household manager turned senior liaison, leverages her meticulous budgeting, event coordination, and public‑speaking prowess to design intergenerational programs at the community center, balancing her love of predictable structure with the flexibility needed to accommodate volunteers’ changing schedules.
info.cultural_background: Tracey was raised in a Midwestern American family with English and German ancestry, embodying many aspects of traditional White American culture such as a strong work ethic, community involvement, and a love for classic holidays. After moving to New York City in her thirties, she embraced the city's vibrant multicultural atmosphere, integrating diverse culinary tastes, arts, and social norms into her daily life while retaining her familial traditions.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Tracey enjoys a lively social calendar that includes weekly swing and salsa dance classes, a women’s book club focused on historical fiction, regular knitting circles, volunteering at a community garden, attending Broadway matinees, participating in cooking classes that explore international cuisines, joining senior travel groups, birdwatching in Central Park, and working on crossword puzzles.
info.sports_persona: Tracey Beagles enjoys low‑impact fitness through swing and salsa dance classes, brisk walks in Central Park while birdwatching, and cheering on the New York Knicks and Yankees, preferring community‑focused activity over competitive sports.
info.arts_persona: Tracey Beagles attends Broadway matinees such as The Lion King, relishes historical fiction by Bernard Cornwell in her women's book club, and dwells in the swing sounds of Ella Fitzgerald and the vibrant brushstrokes of Van Gogh, finding inspiration for her knitting designs.
info.travel_persona: Tracey Beagles participates in senior travel groups that have taken her to historic sites like Gettysburg, Williamsburg, and the Grand Canyon, while she also dreams of revisiting the cobblestone streets of Florence and exploring Kyoto’s temples, planning trips with a structured itinerary but allowing spontaneous photo stops.
info.culinary_persona: Tracey Beagles, an avid home chef, perfects international dishes such as Spanish paella, Thai green curry, and Moroccan tagine, delighting in ingredients like saffron, lemongrass, and smoked paprika, and confidently scales recipes to feed her large community garden potluck while occasionally forgetting to tend the soup on the stove.

info.persona: Leandro Ramirez balances methodical planning with hands‑on curiosity, devoting evenings to cooking, soccer, and strategic gaming, while maintaining a disciplined budget and proactively managing modest health issues.
info.professional_persona: Leandro Ramirez is an aspiring automotive service technician, merging meticulous project‑planning, bilingual fluency, and hands‑on repair skills to deliver reliable service while balancing curiosity with practical problem‑solving, and they consistently follow through on commitments.
info.cultural_background: Leandro is a second‑generation Mexican American who grew up in San Gabriel, a city with a vibrant Latino community. He was raised in a bilingual household where Spanish was spoken daily, and his family maintains strong ties to Mexican traditions such as Día de los Muertos, Cinco de Mayo, and Christmas posadas. The values of familismo, respect for elders, and community solidarity shape his outlook. While embracing his heritage—through food, music, and celebration—he also navigates the multicultural landscape of Southern California, blending Mexican cultural practices with broader American norms. This bicultural identity informs his social network, his commitment to community service, and his aspiration to give back to the Mexican‑American community.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In his downtime, Leandro enjoys a mix of social and solitary activities that reflect his balanced personality. He regularly plays soccer with a neighborhood league, and he finds relaxation in cooking traditional Mexican dishes such as tacos, tamales, and pozole for family gatherings. He also likes tinkering with DIY home‑improvement projects, from building simple furniture to installing smart‑home devices. When alone, he reads science‑fiction and fantasy novels, and he unwinds with strategy video games. Music is a constant backdrop—he listens to regional Mexican, cumbia, and contemporary Latin pop. He volunteers at local cultural festivals, helping with logistics and event setup.
info.sports_persona: Leandro Ramirez plays forward in a neighborhood soccer league, trains twice a week at a local gym, avidly supports FC Dallas, and they also follow the NBA’s Dallas Mavericks during the season, balancing competitive sport with casual fitness.
info.arts_persona: Leandro Ramirez’s soundtrack includes regional cumbia, contemporary Latin pop artists like Juanes and Shakira, occasional indie folk from The Lumineers, and they frequently attend community cultural festivals where local bands perform, letting music shape their leisure and social gatherings.
info.travel_persona: Leandro Ramirez prefers short road trips to national parks such as Grand Canyon and Zion, enjoys attending vibrant street festivals in Austin and New Orleans, and they dream of visiting the historic plazas of Oaxaca and the coastal towns of Portugal for a blend of culture and adventure.
info.culinary_persona: Leandro Ramirez loves cooking classic dishes like tacos, tamales, and pozole, mastering flavors with corn masa, hominy, pork, and chilies, and they experiment with spice blends while also grilling marinated carne asada for friends, showcasing a hands‑on approach to traditional cuisine.
